Text to Lattice security model

Assets, trust boundaries, twelve consequential threats, as-built controls, release qualification gates, and residuals—classified by marginal value.

DocumentationConcept mapSystem skill mapService blueprintSecurity model

Claim boundary

Authority stays typed

This register describes the Lattice method at an architectural level and the bounded Text to Lattice implementation evidenced in this repository. It does not redistribute the exclusive register profile, certify universal conformance, or convert source tests into deployed proof.

Stable identifiers persist. A claim changes here with cited evidence; a rendered filter, expansion, or downloaded view never changes authoritative state.

Markdown and HTML are deterministic projections of this register. Filtered browser exports are nonauthoritative reading views.

As-built source model

Not a penetration test or deployed attestation

Threat model for the active hah.dev Text to Lattice remote capability: deliberate browser submission, content-free visitor-session setup and one content request under the same origin-wide Web Lock, same-origin API validation, fixed server-side Hugging Face, DeepInfra and Nscale processing, bounded response handling, and application-level nonretention. Historical WebLLM, Turnstile, and lease controls are inactive and cannot satisfy this model.

Prioritize controls where consequence, realistic plausibility, and lifecycle reuse are jointly high. Preserve uncomfortable residuals: probabilistic semantic drift, external-provider processing and retention, public-endpoint abuse, output capture, supply-chain change, and the gap between source checks and production evidence.

Decision rule: marginal value is proportional to consequence × plausibility × lifecycle value. Unusual findings remain eligible; novelty alone neither promotes nor dismisses them.

Trust boundaries

  • TB-01

    Visitor prose and browser UI

    Untrusted authorized prose becomes inert local state; only an explicit external-processing action may authorize transmission.

  • TB-02

    Browser and same-origin /api/lattice

    After explicit confirmation, one bodyless setup establishes or preserves the signed cookie without quota or provider work; under the same Web Lock exactly one content POST carries text, requested_mode, and schema_version 1. The browser accepts only bounded closed success or error envelopes.

  • TB-03

    API Worker and Hugging Face router

    Server-created prompts cross only to the fixed chat-completions endpoint with a server-only credential and fixed DeepInfra-served generator and Nscale-served verifier roles.

  • TB-04

    Bounded request memory and persistence surfaces

    Source, prompts, candidates, results, and raw provider bodies may exist transiently in request memory but have no application database, object store, cache, queue, raw-content log, or analytics sink.

  • TB-05

    Provider response and public result

    Closed structured output, deterministic fail-closed host validation, size ceilings, and text-only rendering separate untrusted provider output from public outcome claims.

  • TB-06

    Source register and generated documentation

    Escaped deterministic projections expose current claims and clearly marked historical evidence but no visitor content, secrets, or private profile inventory.

Explore this register

The complete register follows. Search, filters, expansion controls, and local Markdown export require JavaScript; no content does.

SEC-01
Content is transmitted without valid authorization or to an undeclared destination · High marginal value
Vector
Open, edit, validation, prefetch, cancellation, implicit submit, setup failure, blocked cookie storage, automatic retry, a user-controlled target, or a client-visible provider call sends content before deliberate confirmation or outside the named path.
Consequence
Sensitive text leaves the browser contrary to the visitor's choice and the public disclosure.
Plausibility
Ordinary UI, transport, and configuration regressions can create premature, duplicate, or misdirected requests.
Lifecycle value
One named capability and one explicit-action boundary remain reusable across interface and provider revisions.
Classification
Unauthorized or misdirected disclosure is high consequence, integration-plausible, and cheaply prevented by exact request construction and deployment probes.
As built
  • The browser capability is fixed to same-origin POST /api/lattice. Under one origin-wide Web Lock it sends a content-free visitor-session setup followed by exactly one content request containing text, requested_mode, and schema_version 1.
  • Open, edit, validation failure, pre-submit dismissal, and cancellation create no setup or transformation request; a transport or non-204 setup failure prevents the content request; if an accepted setup's HttpOnly cookie is blocked or dropped, the Worker rejects the content request before admission or provider work; terminal failures do not automatically retry.
  • The Worker alone calls the fixed Hugging Face endpoint and fixed DeepInfra-served generator and Nscale-served verifier identifiers.
Required before publication
  • Verify zero network requests before explicit submission on the exact deployed artifact.
  • Capture one successful deployed sequence and the accepted-setup/cookie-blocked failure path; confirm the setup is content-free, exactly one content request follows an accepted setup under the same lock, and the browser contacts only same-origin /api/lattice while Worker egress remains fixed.
Residual boundary
  • The authorized content request necessarily transmits content to Hugging Face, DeepInfra, Nscale, and their infrastructure.
  • Browser extensions, security software, DNS, networks, and provider infrastructure remain outside hah.dev control.

SEC-02
Hostile prose or provider output acquires authority or execution · High marginal value
Vector
Prompt injection, control characters, bidi abuse, HTML-like content, or provider-authored issue text becomes an instruction, executable markup, semantic authority, or generated-document markup.
Consequence
The pipeline can ignore its contract, misrepresent a finding, execute injected content, or expose unsafe markup.
Plausibility
Directly plausible because arbitrary prose and probabilistic provider output are intended inputs.
Lifecycle value
Inert serialization, closed schemas, host-authored public fields, and text-only rendering protect future model and document revisions.
Classification
The input and provider boundaries are necessarily hostile, so containment is a primary release condition.
As built
  • Complete Unicode and structural preflight occurs before the provider pipeline.
  • System instructions are separated from serialized user data. Verification requests a dedicated JSON-object assistant content channel without tools or tool_choice, and accepts only stop-finished content under its minimal envelope guard: absent tool_calls or an independently opted-in empty array or literal null, no legacy function_call, and the metadata fields name and reasoning_content only when literally null. The literal-null collection exception is enabled only for this exact dedicated verifier JSON-object channel following actual S02N evidence. A nonempty tool collection, every other nonarray collection, non-null metadata or any other extra field is rejected; neither message nor content is rewritten. Certification retains one exact named call as authoritative or its explicitly enabled minimal stopped assistant envelope with absent tool fields or an empty tool_calls array, without the verification-only null metadata allowance. Generic defaults are unchanged. Bounded complete JSON and exact fitted closed decoding and host semantics remain mandatory; auxiliary provider prose is never interpreted.
  • Public issue categories are host-controlled and React and documentation generators escape untrusted text.
Required before publication
  • Re-run injection, Unicode, recursive noninterference, malformed-provider-response, and documentation-escaping checks on the release artifact.
  • Review any new renderer, logging hook, response transport, compatibility path, or model transport for HTML interpretation or dynamic authority.
Residual boundary
  • A fixed model can still misunderstand inert data; later semantic gates contain but cannot eliminate that risk.

SEC-03
Semantic drift is released as success · High marginal value
Vector
Generation drops, invents, negates, broadens, narrows, or reorders a material obligation and a correlated checker accepts the candidate.
Consequence
Safety instructions, conditions, quantities, uncertainty, causality, consequences, or recovery relationships change while the interface claims success.
Plausibility
Probabilistic server-side generation makes drift realistic even with structured output.
Lifecycle value
A distinct verifier, deterministic sentinels, source-grounded reanalysis, and honest withholding remain useful across provider revisions.
Classification
Meaning preservation is the product's central consequence; incorrect success is worse than refusal.
As built
  • Protected spans and semantic sentinels preserve explicit high-consequence content.
  • Fixed Qwen generation is checked by fixed Llama verification, deterministic validators, source-grounded reanalysis, bounded repair, and whole-document certification. An identity-owned D14 finding for the same passage under a rewrite plan sets normalized materiality to false before verifier issue and decision consistency. The host supplies a binding negative from its existing deterministic check, never positive semantic acceptance. This negative is carried into the existing bounded repair feedback. Unowned, cloned, other-passage and retained-plan findings cannot supply it; unsupported contradictions without D14 still fail closed. A copied repair remains withheld, and a material repair still requires independent reverification and applicable certification. A restored D14 candidate may consequently receive the existing semantic-rejection held diagnostic category; that classification supplies no public success claim. A separate bounded recovery may repair an authentic D14 nonmaterial rewrite after unavailable initial verification only when the identity-owned terminal record is attempt 2 and both response-shape failures are wire-decoder/coverage V16M or V17M, with D14-only findings bound to current rewrite passages. The repair receives verification null rather than unavailable placeholder checks; it must earn fresh deterministic and full independent verification plus applicable certification. This uses the existing repair opportunity, never supplies missing support or positive semantic acceptance, and cannot be enabled by copied diagnostics, other failures, or mixed findings. Current v12 qualification diagnostics refine only an already-rejected passage failed-check width into V14LE (empty), V14LS (nonempty short) or V14LG (long), all wire-decoder/value-domain. Legacy V14L remains the undifferentiated width predicate for retained evidence. Existing identity-bound tuples carry these finite observations without raw masks, exact nonzero lengths, new fields or new headers. All variants retain the existing mask-width correction request and rejection behavior. No positive verification, new repair eligibility or release claim follows from a width observation.
  • Five outcome states prevent withheld or unresolved work from being relabeled as complete; remote clarification is disabled.
Required before publication
  • Run the full adversarial and semantic regression corpus against the exact remote release revisions.
  • Record manual review across realistic genres without treating samples as universal proof.
Residual boundary
  • No bounded corpus or fixed model pair proves equivalence for all prose.
  • Review-required is semantically releasable but explicitly not complete bounded clearance.

SEC-04
Input or remote inference exhausts bounded resources · High marginal value
Vector
Pathological Unicode, oversized JSON, dense passages, excessive completions, stalled provider calls, repair loops, oversized responses, repeated ordinary-browser use, or distributed valid requests consume bounded browser, Worker, provider, or account resources.
Consequence
The interaction hangs, legitimate visitors exhaust the exact daily admission, provider spend exceeds the intended demonstration budget, or a response exceeds safe client handling.
Plausibility
Realistic for arbitrary public input and third-party inference.
Lifecycle value
Atomic daily admission, centralized ceilings, identity minimization, and fail-closed deadlines bound future pipeline stages and provider revisions.
Classification
Public arbitrary input and paid external work make resource exhaustion ordinary and consequential; an exact global cap has high value even though a cookie-jar limit cannot identify a person.

  • the release decision is machine-checked against the exact source set
  • deployment actions are immutable-revision pinned

GATE-02 · Open Release Blocker · High marginal value

Remote API origin, secret, and privacy boundary

Before public activation, the deployed hah.dev origin must expose exactly one named same-origin POST /api/lattice capability. After explicit confirmation and under one origin-wide browser Web Lock, the canonical client must first send a bodyless visitor-session setup with Accept application/vnd.hah.text-to-lattice-visitor-session.v1+json and no Content-Type, then after an accepted 204 setup send exactly one content-bearing request with schema version 1 and only text, requested_mode, and schema_version in its body. A transport or non-204 setup failure must stop before the content request. Client script cannot observe storage of the HttpOnly cookie, so an accepted 204 whose cookie is blocked or dropped may still be followed by that one content request; the Worker must reject a missing cookie as 428 visitor_session_required before Durable Object admission or provider work, while invalid or undeclared cookies fail closed as 403 invalid_request at the same boundary. The setup must establish or preserve the signed cookie without a quota claim or provider call. The API Worker must use exactly the encrypted HF_TOKEN and VISITOR_COOKIE_SECRET bindings; a first isolated setup has no Cookie header, the following content request may carry only the signed opaque __Secure-hah-lattice-api-visitor cookie, and the setup response sets only that cookie with Path=/api/lattice, Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, no Domain, and expiry at the next UTC-day boundary. No cookie value may enter retained evidence. The Worker must also use the fixed Hugging Face router with the DeepInfra-qualified Qwen generator and Nscale-qualified Llama verifier/certifier targets, exact fitted strict JSON Schema review requests and minimal stopped role/content review envelopes, bounded non-reflective errors, Cache-Control: no-store, no application content storage or logging, no automatic retry, no alternate provider or model fallback, and a Content-Security-Policy whose connect-src is 'self'.

Rationale: Raw visitor text leaves the browser at this boundary and a server credential authorizes external model calls. Route, schema, destination, logging, caching, and error-policy drift therefore have high privacy and cost consequences. Source controls are necessary but cannot establish the deployed route, binding, edge response, or provider behavior.

GATE-03 · Open Release Blocker · High marginal value

Remote provider capacity and cost boundary

The bodyless visitor-session setup must make no quota claim and no provider call. A content request with no cookie must fail 428 visitor_session_required, while one with an invalid, tampered, or undeclared cookie must fail 403 invalid_request, before Durable Object admission or provider work in either case. After exact content-request validation and before provider work, the deployed API must make exactly one atomic admission claim and accept at most 30 transformations globally per UTC day and 3 per cooperating canonical client with an ordinary persistent browser cookie jar per UTC day. Intentional cookie clearing and uncooperative callers remain outside the per-browser identity claim; the global 30-per-day counter remains exact and authoritative. An admitted attempt counts even if its caller disconnects or provider work later fails; it is never refunded and encounters no second shared quota claim within its pipeline. Quota identity and state use no IP address, browser fingerprint, submitted content, or result. Each admitted request permits at most 32 provider calls, so admitted requests expose at most 960 provider calls per UTC day. The path-scoped Worker rate limiter remains a 30-per-60-second edge shaper. Analysis, candidate, certification, and repair calls must each be bounded to 120 seconds, verification to 180 seconds, and the authoritative whole request to 240 seconds so it may end any stage sooner; response size remains bounded, with no paid or generic proxy path and no promise of provider rate, retention, availability, or cost behavior.

Rationale: A public content-bearing endpoint can multiply model calls and cost even when application storage is absent. The exact global admission cap authoritatively bounds accepted work even when a caller clears or partitions the ordinary-browser quota cookie, while the browser limit still reduces ordinary repeated use. A missing or non-atomic production binding, quota or UTC-rollover drift, refund or in-pipeline recheck, identity expansion, provider-bound mismatch, or generic escape path would be consequential. This gate stays open until the deployed boundary is observed.

Architecture: Durable Object lease admission and public Turnstile testing profile

Historical current evidence (verbatim): Deterministic source contracts bound per-visitor and global admission, lease lifetime, retry behavior, row lifecycle, and fail-closed provider errors. Under the public reusable testing token, however, one client can use the permitted 16-request acquisition sequence to fill all eight slots and renew them; the 48-per-10-second per-IP rule does not stop that sequence. The controls bound cost, state, and privacy consequence, not tool availability, and source cannot establish live provider capacity.

Historical evidence record (verbatim):

  • workers/text-to-lattice-lease/policy.js
  • workers/text-to-lattice-lease/usageStorage.js
  • workers/text-to-lattice-lease/retryPolicy.js
  • tests/lattice-protocol-capacity.test.mjs

Evidence needed: After a reviewed deployment, verify the atomic Durable Object admission binding and the 30-per-60-second edge shaper are both present and fail closed before provider work. Prove that visitor-session setup and preservation make no quota claim or provider call, missing-cookie content fails 428 visitor_session_required, invalid, tampered, or undeclared-cookie content fails 403 invalid_request before admission or provider work, and one claim occurs per exactly validated content request. Prove 30 accepted transformations globally per UTC day, 3 per cooperating canonical client with an ordinary persistent browser cookie jar per UTC day, UTC-day rollover, count-on-admission without refund after disconnect or provider failure, and no second shared quota claim within an admitted pipeline. Record intentional cookie clearing and uncooperative callers outside the per-browser identity claim while proving the exact global counter remains authoritative. Confirm quota identity and state contain no IP address, browser fingerprint, submitted content, or result; record the 32-provider-call per-admission ceiling and resulting 960-call maximum daily provider exposure; record bounded production-representative timeout, rate-limit, malformed-response, latency, and cost behavior; confirm no generic proxy or paid fallback path; and record external provider retention and availability as unguaranteed. Retain observed abuse or cost drift as a requalification trigger.

Safeguards:

  • content-free visitor-session setup and preservation make no quota claim or provider call; missing-cookie content fails 428 and invalid, tampered, or undeclared-cookie content fails 403 before admission or provider work
  • one atomic Durable Object claim after exact content validation and before provider work enforces 30 accepted transformations globally per UTC day and 3 per cooperating canonical client with an ordinary persistent browser cookie jar per UTC day; intentional cookie clearing and uncooperative callers remain outside the per-browser identity claim while the global counter stays exact
  • the API route also has a 30-per-60-second path-scoped rate-limiter binding as an edge shaper
  • admitted attempts count on disconnect or provider failure without refund, and their pipelines perform no second shared quota claim
  • quota identity and state contain no IP address, browser fingerprint, submitted content, or result
  • provider calls are bounded to 32 per admitted request and 960 from admitted requests per UTC day; response bytes, response characters, and total stage count are also bounded
  • provider timeouts and malformed responses fail closed without reflection
  • there is no browser retry, alternate provider fallback, model fallback, or generic proxy parameter
  • the public copy promises no availability and identifies provider retention as external

GATE-04A · Accepted Residual Risk · Moderate marginal value

Llama behavior and public-use controls

The public flow discloses model assistance and known limitations, obtains a source-specific lawful-and-authorized-use confirmation, defines prohibited-use safety by purpose and consequence, withholds any safety-failing candidate, and tests realistic harmful and legitimate-context cases.

Rationale: The public-use controls address realistic misuse and misunderstanding. Exact provider-served model fixture execution would improve empirical confidence; a verifier false negative remains unobserved and candidate withholding depends on the verifier's classification. Source-specific confirmation, error and explicit-denial withholding, a fixed server-side response pipeline with no user-selectable tools, and mandatory human review bound the official product surface without proving classifier behavior.

Current evidence: The active Llama 3.1 terms snapshots and attribution match the reviewed model-repository files. Source implements point-of-use disclosure, resettable source-specific confirmation, purpose-and-consequence safety, and candidate suppression, with deterministic regressions and a balanced ten-case non-operational fixture. Exact-model behavioral evidence was reset for meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct:nscale; this environment does not contain a recorded execution and manual review of that fixture against the active verifier.

Rationale: A substituted verifier artifact would be consequential, so immutable identity and controlling terms remain mandatory. The missing publisher conversion narrative is a real but moderate custody gap after those controls, not a demonstrated incompatible or malicious artifact.

Historical inactive current evidence: The verifier repository and revision are pinned and the controlling base-model terms are present; the MLC artifact repository does not provide a complete conversion and artifact-license record.

Acceptance basis: The exact artifact identity and base-model terms are known, but hashes do not establish the converted artifact's own authorization or notice custody; that gap remains explicitly accepted for this bounded browser-local demonstrator, which retrieves the immutable publisher-hosted artifact rather than redistributing its shards from hah.dev. Exact SHA-256, SRI, git-blob, repository, revision, ABI, and configuration bindings materially reduce substitution and compatibility risk; pursuing theoretical reconstruction of every unavailable historical input would add substantial complexity without a plausible proportional failure reduction.

The binary repository has no root license at the reviewed revision; the historical helper is workstation-specific, calls a Qwen preset absent from the recorded MLC revision, leaves Python and Cargo inputs unlocked, and has no matching independent rebuild.

Acceptance basis: Exact identity and compatibility controls reduce technical substitution and incompatibility risk. They do not establish artifact-level authorization or notice custody; that separate gap remains explicitly accepted for this bounded browser-local demonstrator, which retrieves exact publisher-hosted libraries rather than redistributing them from hah.dev. A full historical reproducible rebuild is negative marginal value for this boundary because it demands bespoke reconstruction and long-term maintenance without a commensurate plausible technical-risk reduction; upstream clarification or a maintainable replacement remains eligible future work.

GATE-06 · Open Release Blocker · High marginal value

Remote production lifecycle and privacy trace

From the activated canonical page in each supported browser engine, one explicit confirmed submission in a first isolated persistent session must acquire one origin-wide browser Web Lock and produce one bodyless content-free same-origin POST /api/lattice setup with Accept application/vnd.hah.text-to-lattice-visitor-session.v1+json, no body or Content-Type, credentials mode same-origin, and no Cookie header. That response must set exactly the __Secure-hah-lattice-api-visitor cookie with Path=/api/lattice, Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, no Domain, and a Max-Age within the next UTC-day boundary. Under the same lock, after an accepted 204 the client must then produce exactly one content-bearing same-origin POST /api/lattice with only text, requested_mode, and schema_version 1 in its body and only that browser-owned cookie, then reach one non-error terminal result (translated, conformant-for-context, or review-required). A transport or non-204 setup failure must stop before the content request. Because script cannot observe HttpOnly-cookie storage, an accepted 204 whose cookie is blocked or dropped may still be followed by that one content request; the missing-cookie request must fail 428 visitor_session_required before admission and provider work. Setup must consume no transformation quota and make no provider call. Neither request carries an account, authorization, or provider credential. The trace must show no provider origin contacted by the browser, no automatic retry, no service-worker replay or cache replay, and no additional content-bearing browser request, and must distinguish the intentionally transmitted request body from prohibited source or result reflection in URLs, headers, errors, logs, caches, analytics, and unrelated traffic. Retained evidence records only value-free cookie metadata and never a cookie value.

Rationale: The migration intentionally moves source text across a new browser/server/provider boundary. A source-correct UI can still fail in deployment, retry unexpectedly, contact a wrong destination, leak content through errors or instrumentation, or produce no terminal result. Canonical-browser evidence is therefore a high-value release prerequisite rather than post-release follow-up.

Architecture: canonical browser-local WebLLM, Turnstile, and lease lifecycle

Historical current evidence (verbatim): The owner supplied sanitized captures from the activated canonical client at https://hah.dev/resume/#text-to-lattice after workflow run https://github.com/howardhayden/folio/actions/runs/34325228788 deployed commit 9ab26b95cc1f9a94697118c0fc20a849db8f6ad2. Safari Version 26.5 (21624.2.5.11.4), WebKit, on macOS 26.5.1 (25F80), M5 iMac, with an operator-normalized capture time of 2026-09-09T08:05:50Z, directly records the first-session sequence POST /api/text-to-lattice/lease 428, the isolated https://verify.hah.dev/turnstile/ frame and Cloudflare challenge resources, POST /api/text-to-lattice/lease 200, and DELETE /api/text-to-lattice/lease 204 with a zero-byte response. Brave 1.94.121 (Chromium 152.0.7977.83, arm64) on the same platform, with operator-normalized capture times from 2026-09-09T08:15:12Z through 2026-09-09T08:22:30Z, independently records the second-engine lease statuses 428, 200, and 204, the isolated verification origin and challenge flow, and pinned Qwen tokenizer and model-asset loading. The deployed canonical-client source correlates those ordered Brave rows to POST 428, POST 200, and DELETE 204; the screenshot itself does not independently prove the later request methods. The owner reports that a capture-wide search for the unique submitted source marker returned 0 matches across the Brave network record. That search establishes the source-specific negative check. The deployed source contract and tests keep source, clarification, candidate, verifier finding, and output browser-local and exclude them from lease, attestation, model-asset, error, or telemetry traffic; the captured request inventory shows no undocumented content-bearing route. The canonical URL, bodyless lease request and release source contracts, and exact Cloudflare official testing profile are additionally bound by the deployed source and operator record rather than inferred from screenshot pixels. Payload-pane inspection was not claimed. The UTC times are operator normalizations of the local capture filenames, not server-signed timestamps. Cloudflare automatically injected a Web Analytics tag for https://static.cloudflareinsights.com/beacon.min.js into both document responses, but each CSP blocked the external beacon resource before transfer or execution (blocked:csp, 0.0 kB), and no /cdn-cgi/rum or other RUM transmission appeared. This composite evidence establishes canonical official-page integration and the observed privacy boundary under the declared testing profile; it does not establish human verification, bot resistance, token freshness or single use, hostname or action assurance, universal browser behavior, or production anti-bot assurance, and it does not establish that Cloudflare Web Analytics is disabled or that ordinary provider transport metadata is absent. Those captures remain historical evidence for the lease lifecycle and observed privacy boundary of their deployed revision; subsequent diagnosis established that the rapid DELETE followed a model-worker import failure and did not demonstrate a terminal conversion. The repair candidate adds a worker-only Vite pre-transform that preserves fourteen bare realm checks across the pinned WebLLM and web-tokenizers modules with fail-closed twelve/two count assertions, plus a final-artifact Worker-realm smoke that boots without window, completes the cached RPC, and reaches the first approved model-configuration cache request without network access. Because this changes emitted runtime behavior, GATE-06 is post-deployment verification: after deployment, repeat the supported-engine lifecycle and sanitized two-origin privacy trace and record one non-error terminal conversion. On 2026-09-11, the site owner reported that the deployed repaired runtime reached a full green progress bar after about one minute but remained at "Preparing on this device" with "Your result will appear here" and produced no terminal result. This owner report establishes the failed observable outcome; it is not a timestamped network capture, does not identify a newly verified deployment revision, and does not replace the historical evidence above. The replacement source candidate requires the exact https://hah.dev browser origin before any lease fetch, so local and Vite previews fail with a canonical-origin explanation instead of requesting a missing local API route. It adds a worker-realm capability probe before lease acquisition or model download; phase-aware WebLLM download, GPU-loading, and shader-compilation progress that becomes nondeterminate after the first completed phase; a closed worker-start acknowledgement so execution deadlines do not run while requests wait in the serialized queue; 30-second worker-start, 120-second preparation-inactivity, 720-second completion-inactivity, and 45-minute hard execution bounds; 15-second adapter and 10-second storage checks; a 30-second lease fetch-and-body deadline; a 10-second browser provenance-digest deadline; and explicit terminal errors. While the resume component remains mounted, Close, backdrop, and Escape are visibility-only in every phase and preserve input, availability or attestation request, lease-bound work, post-request processing, clarification, error, terminal state, and result for reopening; Cancel and Start over terminate or reset the current request, and component unmount tears it down; completion and error may release runtime resources, but their terminal state remains reopenable. The response-policy candidate preserves or adds Cache-Control: no-transform, and the live verifier now uses browser-shaped navigation requests and rejects conditionally injected Cloudflare beacon or RUM markers. These are source controls awaiting deployment verification; they do not establish that Cloudflare Web Analytics or RUM is disabled and do not establish a successful production conversion.

  • GATE-02 and GATE-03 must close before activation
  • the trace must originate from the canonical public client and bind one deployed revision
  • the request sequence is explicit, same-origin, no-store, and never automatically retried; one origin-wide Web Lock spans the bodyless setup and, after accepted 204, exactly one exact-schema content request; transport or non-204 failure stops before content, while blocked or dropped HttpOnly-cookie storage after accepted 204 is observable only through the Worker's 428 pre-admission rejection
  • the first isolated setup has no body, Content-Type, or Cookie header, exposes only the exact non-secret Set-Cookie attributes in retained evidence, and the following content request may carry only that signed API-scoped cookie
  • setup consumes no transformation quota and contacts no provider; missing-cookie content fails 428 before admission or provider work
  • account, authorization, and provider credentials are absent; provider origin and credentials remain server-only and there is no alternate provider or model fallback
  • bounded non-reflective failures cannot echo source, prompt, provider body, or result
  • the retained trace summary excludes raw HAR data, cookie values, bearer values, provider credentials, submitted source, generated output, raw bodies, and sensitive headers

Follow-up: Keep the public client held until the required qualification-expiry-bound canonical-browser records exist. Repeat the functional and privacy trace after any consequential route, setup envelope, Web Lock, schema, cookie, provider, model, response, CSP, cache, retention, telemetry, interaction, timeout, or retry-policy change.

Rollback condition: Keep GATE-06 open and the public client held, or return it immediately to held documentation-only publication, if a canonical trace lacks one non-error terminal result; lacks the bodyless custom-Accept setup; emits a content request after transport or non-204 setup failure; emits more or fewer than one intended content-bearing POST /api/lattice after accepted 204; does not hold one browser Web Lock across setup and the full content response; sends a body, Content-Type, or Cookie on the first isolated setup; omits or drifts the exact value-free Set-Cookie metadata; sends an undeclared cookie or any account, authorization, or provider credential; lets setup consume quota or contact the provider; lets accepted-204 content with a blocked, dropped, or missing cookie reach admission or provider work instead of returning 428 visitor_session_required; retains a cookie value; contacts a provider from the browser; retries automatically; uses a cache or service worker; outlives the bound qualification expiry; or reflects source, prompts, provider bodies, findings, or output outside the acknowledged request and bounded result.

Honest residual boundary

  • The authorized request necessarily sends submitted content and server-created prompts to Hugging Face, DeepInfra, Nscale, and their infrastructure under external policies; hah.dev's application nonretention rule does not guarantee provider retention or deletion behavior.
  • Qwen generation and Llama verification are probabilistic. Closed schemas, deterministic sentinels, independent model roles, bounded repair, and honest withholding reduce but do not eliminate semantic drift.
  • Provider-managed serving is not byte-pinned or byte-equivalent to the historical MLC WebLLM artifacts. Fixed hosted identifiers do not prove immutable weights, tokenizer bytes, infrastructure, or serving implementation.
  • The 3-per-day claim applies only to the cooperating canonical client with an ordinary persistent cookie jar. Intentional cookie clearing or uncooperative callers can rotate that identity, while the exact global 30-per-day admission remains authoritative; distributed traffic can still exhaust that finite capacity.
  • Browser output controls deter routine copying but cannot prevent screenshots, cameras, privileged extensions, developer tools, accessibility APIs, or memory access.
  • Repository source and tests do not prove deployed routes, encrypted secret bindings, edge response behavior, live-provider behavior, external retention, representative accessibility, or a successful canonical-browser lifecycle.
  • Historical WebLLM, Turnstile, lease, artifact, and production-trace evidence remains useful design history but is inactive and cannot qualify the remote candidate.
  • DeepInfra serves the fixed generator and Nscale serves the fixed verifier/certifier in this candidate. Model-role and host validation do not establish provider isolation, immutable serving bytes, inference-body zero retention or no training. Public provider documents are not a negotiated service agreement or DPA; exact-provider production and canonical-browser evidence remain open.
